newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says unlikely to tap Japan Exim loan.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says unlikely to tap Japan Exim loan.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday the country was not likely to draw from the $400 million parallel financing facility of the Japan Export-Import Bank.
"We do not see the need to be looking at the Japanese Exim financing because the central bank has the IMF financing and the peso is stabilising," de Ocampo told reporters.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) approved on Friday the release of an existing $652 million loan to the Philippines and an additional $435 million to help ease the problems caused by its recent currency turmoil.
The Japan Eximbank financing is tied to the IMF programme which was entered into in 1994 but was never availed of due to the Philippines' healthy international reserves.
The final decision on whether to tap the Japanese financing rests on the Monetary Board of the central bank.
